text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Traffic was slowed down across the country yesterday, but there were no major tie-ups as farmers began three days of demonstrations to protest against the government's latest taxation and social insurance contribution measures. Negotiations between farmers and the cabinet looked set to begin today.
- Visiting German President Roman Herzog yesterday pledged full support from Germany for Hungary's Euro-Atlantic integration aspirations.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said Monday extremist parties are trying to capitalise on the current farmers' demonstrations for their own ends, adding that the cabinet is ready to negotiate with farmers' representatives.
- State privatisation agency APV supervisory board president Sandor Puskas is stepping down of his own volition, he announced, adding his move has nothing to do with the Tocsik case.
- Socialist MP Katalin Ilona Aszodi, who was elected on an individual ticket in the Kiskoros constituency, announced that she is quitting the Socialist Party for moral reasons.
- Mayors of 21 towns along the M5 motorway and related interest groups threatened to organise a demonstration on March 8 unless the toll on the motorway is cut by half.
- Unidentified thieves entered the office of Democratic Forum president Sandor Lezsak in the parliamentary office building on the weekend and removed his computer, a printer and a personal database.
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy proposed that Prime Minister Gyula Horn ask the State Audit Office to carry out a detailed investigation of the losses at Polgari Bank.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The World Trade Organisation will set up a dispute settlement panel today to rule on the question of Hugnary's agricultural export subsidies.

- Ikarus president Gabor Szeles outlined ways of managing the company's huge debts yesterday, now that the bus maker has been retrieved from the brink of collapse, Ikarus may be able to turn to profit this year.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Plans for NATO expansion were among topics discussed at a meeting between Slovak Defence Minister Jan Sitek and his Hungarian counterpart Gyorgy Keleti in Budapest yesterday.
- Michael Colvin, chairman of the defence committee in the British House of Commons, yesterday opened two days of talks in Budapest with Hungarian political and military leaders.
- The Nethold TV company which owns the FilmNet cable channel is withdrawing from Eastern Europe.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- A Partnership for Peace air defence exercise is underway in Kecskemet until February 27.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Two bids have come in from Franco-German consortia for 25 percent plus one share of the Capital Water Works in the second round of the company's privatisation.
- The public may purchase the Pannon GSM bonds issued last week from Thursday this week.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Brake manufacturer Knorr-Bremse Kft closed last year with profits of 84 milion forints on sales of 3.568 billion forints.
